restrictions: Typing was exercised with Win32 messages, not by a person with a real keyboard: the Edit control received EM_SETSEL then the WM_CHAR messages M, a, r, i, e (SendMessageW from another process) and the Static control was read back with WM_GETTEXT ("Bonjour Marie", 16.3 ms after the first message on x64, 15.4 ms on x86, an upper bound for the update delay compared with the 1 s of User Story 1). Real key events, the focus and caret behaviour, input methods (IME), clipboard paste and drag and drop were not tested. The 1,000-character limit was checked by sending 1,100 WM_CHAR messages (EM_GETLIMITTEXT 1000, Edit length 1000); text given by --probe-input bypasses that limit and is cut by the application itself.

The end-of-life warning (FR-013, ui-contract item 3) was not exercised: Windows 11 26H2 is in support (validation/sources.json eol-windows-11), so eol_warning_shown was false in all 40 probe runs and no banner exists in the window (one Static only). The check 'warning on every end-of-life system' of T088 has no case on this platform; the only earlier display of the banner (T073) was with a test-only build reporting Windows 7, outside this trial.

No skipped-feature path was exercised: every optional feature (dark mode, DPI awareness, high-contrast query, GetProcessMemoryInfo) exists on Windows 11, so disabled_features was empty in all 40 probe runs and the fallbacks of validation/fallbacks.json were never taken. disabled_features is therefore recorded empty for Windows 11 only.

Only the default appearance was looked at: light theme (AppsUseLightTheme = 1), high contrast off (high-contrast flags 126, HCF_HIGHCONTRASTON not set), system DPI 96 (100%). The dark theme, a high-contrast scheme, DPI scaling above 100%, per-monitor DPI and the dark title bar were not exercised in this trial, and the 4.5:1 contrast ratio of ui-contract item 2 was not measured on the captured pixels (the controls use the system colours).

The screenshots are PrintWindow captures of the window (420x200, title bar included, empty shadow corners), not screen recordings and not an independent view of the physical screen; 'displayed' and display_ms in the probe record come from the application's own first WM_PAINT. The glyph rendering of the non-ASCII vectors (accents, CJK, right-to-left, emoji, combining characters) was not looked at: tools/run_vectors.py checks the text of the probe line, not what the fonts of this system draw; only "Coucou" and "Marie" were seen in captures.

Only one Windows version and one machine: Windows 11 26H2 (10.0.26300.9974), French (fr-FR), x64, on a physical MSI laptop whose Windows runs on top of the Microsoft hypervisor. Not tested: Windows 11 ARM64, Windows 10 and every older Windows (8.1, 7, Vista, XP, 2000), a native 32-bit Windows (the x86 exe only ran under WOW64 on this 64-bit system, which is why it reports platform_id windows-11-x64 like the x64 exe), other languages, other machines or virtualised hosts. Timings and memory are those of this laptop, from 20 runs per executable (plus 15 vector runs each), enough for a min / median / max, not for a distribution.

This trial says nothing about the Legacy floor: Windows 11 is the newest system of the Windows Legacy ladder and the 'oldest working Windows' of FR-005 / SC-002 / SC-009 is not determined by it. The Windows 2000 SP4 / XP / Vista / 7 / 8.1 / 10 runs of T088, spike S1 (T066) and the 'verify' entries of the import allowlist remain open; no run of either executable on a system older than this Windows 11 is recorded.

No procedure document exists yet for this trial (validation/procedures/windows.md is task T109), so the verdict carries no 'reproduction' path; the commands used are in the 'notes' field and the driver script is part of the evidence.

The executables were started from a scratch copy in the Windows temp folder (one copy per run) so that loomora-probe.json files could not collide; they were built by 'wsl -d Ubuntu-24.04 -- python3 tools/build.py windows legacy' (up to date, sha256 below) and closed by a WM_CLOSE message, not by a click on the close button. The deliverable record of this platform is validation/deliverables/windows-11-x64-legacy.json (the x64 executable; the x86 executable that was also run here under WOW64 is named in its notes), written by 'tools/build.py windows legacy' from the platform record.

notes: Windows 11 trial of the Windows Legacy UI, on the physical host described in validation/platforms/windows-11-x64.json, 2026-11-12. It covers only the Windows 11 part of T088 and the Windows 11 evidence of T094; it says nothing about the Legacy floor (Windows 2000) and does not determine the oldest working Windows (FR-005). Commands (repository root, Windows host): 'wsl -d Ubuntu-24.04 --cd <repo> -- python3 tools/build.py windows legacy' (up to date), 'python tools/trials/windows-11-x64/trial-driver.py' (40 probe runs, two window runs, host measurements), then 'python tools/run_vectors.py windows-11-x64 legacy --arch x64 --evidence-dir validation/evidence/<change>/windows-11-x64/' and the same with '--arch x86'. The x86 executable ran under WOW64 and reports the id of the operating system architecture (windows-11-x64); the Windows launcher of tools/run_vectors.py copies the exe to a scratch folder per run, starts it through CreateProcess with an argument list (UTF-16 command line built by Python), waits for the exit and reads loomora-probe.json; its 1,000-character expectation counts UTF-16 units (a character outside the BMP counts as two and is never cut), which no current vector exercises (checked once with a temporary vectors file outside the repository: 999 'a' + emoji gives 999 units kept, 998 'a' + emoji gives 1000). The text files of this evidence folder must keep their LF line endings (validation/evidence/.gitattributes marks them -text) because the verdict holds their sha256.
